title: AI APIs and Integrations
answer: Endpoints, SDKs, authentication, rate limits, pricing, uptime, and changelogs for every public AI API.

reading.body:
The API layer of AI is documented as four things: endpoints, pricing, uptime, and the serving providers that run the inference. The serving provider list is the only part tied to physical location.

The other three sections describe commercial and operational surface. Endpoints, SDKs, authentication, rate limits, billing, and changelogs tell you how a developer reaches a model and what it costs. None of that reveals where the computation happens or what it draws from the grid.

The serving provider directory is different. It records headquarters country and datacenter regions for over 100 providers, sourced daily from the OpenRouter routing catalog. That is the join between an API call and a building: jurisdiction follows the datacenter, and jurisdiction determines which rules apply, including the EU AI Act, data residency requirements, and export controls.

What the data does not contain is any count of APIs, any price, any uptime figure, or any named provider. The total is zero and the points list is empty, so the structure is described but not populated here. Treat this as a map of what the API layer consists of, not as evidence about its current state.
